steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until crisp, about 10 minutes. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel-lined plate; return the skillet with the reserved bacon grease to the stove.

Cook the onion in the bacon drippings until soft, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the green beans and red pepper flakes; cook another 2 minutes. Pour the boiling water into the skillet and cover the skillet immediately; steam for about 15 minutes, shaking the skillet occasionally to keep the beans from sticking to the bottom. Add the butter, lemon juice, salt, and pepper; cook and stir until the butter is melted, 3 to 5 minutes. Sprinkle the cooked bacon over the beans to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultimate Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: Tired of green bean casserole? Try this fresh green bean dish that is worthy of the holidays!

review.reviewBody: Wow. These were really delicious and so easy to prepare. Next time I will probably omit the butter as it didn’t really add to the taste but it did add to the calories.

I have been making this recipe for a long time, but an easier way is to cook the bacon with the onions, dry on paper towel, save til later. Steam the fresh green beans with garlic salt and pepper until dark green but still crispy. Pour water out from steamer or double broiler, return beans to the pan and add the bacon onion mixture, stiring until blended. Add some sliced almond on top. I also make these with redskins in one pan as they show on the picture. The bacon seeps into the potatoes and it is a meal in itself.

I made a few changes, but I think the core of the recipe is very sound!

Call me crazy, but I really like to sautee tofu in bacon grease. This way I get a lot of meaty, tasty flavor without actually eating as much meat. So I used three bacon slices, then added diced tofu to the pan at the onion stage, then removed it (left it with the bacon), and continued the recipe as written. It was much more filling and made a casual main meal. The second time I made it, I made it the same as the first time (with the tofu) and just for fun added some diced ginger, which I thought was very tasty. Serve with cauliflower rice for a nice paleo meal.

Really amazing green beans, but not for the faint of heart when it comes to fat. I cooked the bacon quite crispy & and only added when I served it. That created a nice crunch. I did reduce the steaming time to about eight minutes; I like my veggies to have crunch.

I will never make "Green Bean Casserole" again! I came here looking for a fresh, more authentic (than canned cream soup) recipe for green beans when I found this one. At first, my teen daughter discouraged me and asked me why I needed a green bean recipe for Thanksgiving in the first place. I am a traditionalist in many ways and just thought it would be nice to have a green bean dish as I'd always had throughout my childhood. Thankfully, I stayed the course and made this recipe. As soon as I tasted it, I quickly sent it out to my friends and family -- it's THAT GOOD! Since I have young children, I did omit the red pepper flakes. However, the lemon juice, which I thought would be trivial, gave it a beautiful and subtle tang that I would have missed out on if I had omitted that. I also added more bacon because, let's be honest, what isn't better with more bacon? ;) (I now see that the amount of bacon had an error with the original posting, so that makes sense!) This is now my traditional Thanksgiving and Christmas green bean recipe, and I'm sure we'll be taking it to pot lucks in the summertime, too. Just love it!
Great make it all the time but, use low sodium chicken broth instead of water gives them a little more flavor

I omitted the red pepper flakes and butter and used chicken broth instead of plain water. The beans were good but still kind of bland. I also added minced garlic with the lemon juice. Next time I will try more salt and that will probably do the trick.

Swapped out the bacon for diced pancetta, either way, it has amazing flavor. The lemon gives it a subtle kick! The 15 mins was too long to cook, making the green beans too soft/soggy. Recommend checking on it after 8-10 mins. Love this recipe!

Wow what a great recipe! I've made these three times in the last couple of weeks. I omitted the lemon because they were so good when done and wasn't sure I'd like it any better with the lemon, I forgot the red pepper flake altogether (just realized that), used more chopped onion than called for bc I love the onion sautéed in the bacon grease, and these were just wonderful with the perfect hint of bacon. There really is no need to add the crumbled up bacon on top which I think could overpower the great taste of the green beans. I found that after adding the boiling water, cooking/steaming them for 15 minutes was too long. I don't necessarily like my beans crisp but cooking for 5 or 6 minutes was plenty. Next time I will try adding in the lemon and pepper flake. Also used frozen green beans which I allowed to thaw (probably didn't have to,) and these were great! Thanks for the great recipe!

This was very bland. I even used chicken broth instead of water. I even added garlic powder to give it more flavor. I did not use the red pepper, don't like heat. I ended up sprinkling on grated Parmesan-Romano-Asiago cheese on top to make it more palatable for us. IF, big IF, I make it again, I will use more bacon. Maybe that will help.
Note: The 2 slices of bacon is a typo, it was originally 2 ounces of slab bacon (although I have used sliced bacon with equally god results as well). Thanks for the reviews!
Not too much ultimate about this. Needs some serious flavor. It did indeed get too mushy after steaming it for so long
Need more flavor
Easy and really good!
Great green bean recipe! Was looking for something simple and not creamy. Topped with a bit of lemon zest too, will do again!
We liked it quite a bit. I would just cut down on the pepper flakes. My husband likes spicey but I'm sensitive a bit.

5.32.22 Really tasty green beans, but please don’t steam for 15 minutes, or you’ll have mushy beans. These only take 3-4 minutes to steam crisp tender. I backed out a star for the timing issue, but if cooked properly, this recipe definitely is worthy of a 5-star rating.
Watch the red pepper flakes
We liked these a lot. I cooked them a few minutes longer to get the green beans tender.
Wonderful recipe. Easy and delicious.
